replacement: My friends, pray to God for gladness. Be glad like children, like the birds of heaven. And do not let men’s sin trouble you in your work. Do not fear that it will wear your work away and keep it from being finished. Do not say, “Sin is mighty, wickedness is mighty, our evil surroundings are mighty, and we are alone and helpless. Our evil surroundings are wearing us away and keeping our good work from being done.” Flee from that gloom, children! There is only one way to be saved. Take the blame on yourself and make yourself answerable for the sins of all men. That is the truth, you know, friends. As soon as you sincerely make yourself answerable for everything and for everyone, you will see at once that it really is so, and that you are to blame for every person and every thing. But if you push your own laziness and weakness onto others, you will end by sharing the pride of Satan and complaining against God.

God took seeds from other worlds and sowed them on this earth. His garden grew, and everything came up that could come up. But whatever grows is alive only through its sense of touching other, mysterious worlds. If that feeling grows weak in you, or is destroyed, the heavenly growth in you will die. Then you will be indifferent to life, and even come to hate it. That is what I think.

In the end the elder’s death came quite unexpectedly. The people gathered around him that last evening knew that his death was near. Still, it was hard to imagine it would come so suddenly. On the contrary, as I said before, his friends saw him that night so seemingly cheerful and talkative that they were convinced his condition had changed for the better, at least for a time. Even five minutes before he died, they said afterwards in amazement, there was no way of foreseeing it. He seemed suddenly to feel a sharp pain in his chest. He went pale and pressed his hands to his heart. Everyone got up from their seats and hurried to him. But though he was in pain, he still looked at them with a smile. He slid slowly from his chair to his knees, then bowed his face to the ground, stretched out his arms, and, as if in joyful ecstasy, praying and kissing the ground, he quietly and joyfully gave up his soul to God.
